original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Reduce repeated directory validation in the complete captured PR6030 selected-baseline command while preserving every source hash, metadata check and output byte under a stable POSIX tree.
scope_change_reason: The card first working example and a complete-command profile identify repeated path resolution and shared-directory symlink checks in explicit_file. This applies the original coverage-preserving runtime objective to the source-bound orientation command rather than auditing a predecessor scientific result.
bottleneck_link: Faster complete source authentication reduces research/review startup cost. It does not alter a recursive invoice, physical caller or multiplication exponent.
stop_rule: Stop at the first measured complete-command improvement with exact output equivalence and alias/corruption controls. Do not extend to new scientific results, persistent caches or production adoption.
evidence: PROOF.md gives stable-tree acceptance and full-command equivalence. Exact direct normal/optimized conformance passes. Five alternating official-command/adapter pairs have identical stdout, zero errors, and 33.67 percent lower local median time. Registered replay and publication evidence are reported in the PR body.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a maintained baseline adopt this optimization with matching POSIX and Windows contracts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The separate adapter does not change the default baseline or establish portable timing.
open_questions.first_step: Run complete conformance and command benchmarks on Linux and Windows before a proposed maintained integration.
open_questions.blocked_by: Native Windows testing, portable performance evidence and adoption are outside this result.

open_questions.question: Can a later selected source closure use the same bounded prefix validator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The package intentionally captures one exact selected record and explicit dependency set.
open_questions.first_step: Capture the later record, enumerate its complete source closure and rerun rejection controls and complete-command measurements.
open_questions.blocked_by: No automatic migration, changed capacity claim or future record support is supplied.
